variants.prompt: From the lesson section “What is a data distribution shift?”: match each part to its responsibility.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A data distribution shift is a change in the joint distribution of model inputs and outcomes between a reference environment and the environment where the model now operates. In plain language, the world reaching the model no longer looks or behaves like the evidence used to build and validate it.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Separate distribution movement from model harm”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Covariate shift
pairs.detail: The input distribution changes while the conditional relationship P(Y|X) is assumed stable.
pairs.explanation: The input distribution changes while the conditional relationship P(Y|X) is assumed stable. A new device mix may change image properties without changing what the labels mean.

pairs.label: Prior probability shift
pairs.detail: The outcome prevalence changes while P(X|Y) is assumed stable.
pairs.explanation: The outcome prevalence changes while P(X|Y) is assumed stable. A seasonal fraud spike can move the positive rate even when within-class patterns remain similar.

pairs.label: Concept drift
pairs.detail: The relationship learned by the model changes.
pairs.explanation: The relationship learned by the model changes. A policy, market, or adversary can make the same input pattern imply a different outcome.

pairs.label: Data quality incident
pairs.detail: A unit, schema, category mapping, timestamp, or join changes unexpectedly.
pairs.explanation: A unit, schema, category mapping, timestamp, or join changes unexpectedly. This can resemble distribution shift, but retraining would encode the defect instead of repairing it.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. To respond safely, connect four kinds of evidence: data contracts and pipeline health; input and prediction distributions; delayed labels and slice-level performance; user or business impact.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Covariate shift: The input distribution changes while the conditional relationship P(Y|X) is assumed stable. Prior probability shift: The outcome prevalence changes while P(X|Y) is assumed stable. Concept drift: The relationship learned by the model changes. Data quality incident: A unit, schema, category mapping, timestamp, or join changes unexpectedly.

pairs.label: Univariate two-sample tests
pairs.detail: For a continuous feature, the two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic measures the largest gap between empirical cumulative distributions.
pairs.explanation: For a continuous feature, the two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic measures the largest gap between empirical cumulative distributions. Pair it with sample counts and an effect-size policy.

pairs.label: Multivariate detection
pairs.detail: A domain classifier asks whether held-out reference and current records are distinguishable.
pairs.explanation: A domain classifier asks whether held-out reference and current records are distinguishable. Validate it out of sample and inspect which slices or features carry the signal.

pairs.label: Performance monitoring
pairs.detail: When outcomes arrive, compare task metrics, calibration, and costs by model version and population slice.
pairs.explanation: When outcomes arrive, compare task metrics, calibration, and costs by model version and population slice. This is stronger evidence of harm than input drift alone.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. To respond safely, connect four kinds of evidence: data contracts and pipeline health; input and prediction distributions; delayed labels and slice-level performance; user or business impact.

Multivariate detection: A domain classifier asks whether held-out reference and current records are distinguishable. Performance monitoring: When outcomes arrive, compare task metrics, calibration, and costs by model version and population slice.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Match the intervention to the diagnosed cause”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Repair the source
pairs.detail: Restore the schema, unit, join, or upstream feed; backfill affected records where possible; and replay predictions only when product semantics permit it.
pairs.explanation: Restore the schema, unit, join, or upstream feed; backfill affected records where possible; and replay predictions only when product semantics permit it.

pairs.label: Contain exposure
pairs.detail: Route to a fallback, narrow the eligible population, require human review, or roll back while evidence and labels are collected.
pairs.explanation: Route to a fallback, narrow the eligible population, require human review, or roll back while evidence and labels are collected.

pairs.label: Recalibrate policy
pairs.detail: Adjust thresholds or calibration when prevalence or decision costs changed but labeled evidence shows the score ordering remains useful.
pairs.explanation: Adjust thresholds or calibration when prevalence or decision costs changed but labeled evidence shows the score ordering remains useful.

pairs.label: Retrain a candidate
pairs.detail: Use representative, quality-checked labels when the learned relationship changed.
pairs.explanation: Use representative, quality-checked labels when the learned relationship changed. Compare against the incumbent on current and protected historical slices.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. To respond safely, connect four kinds of evidence: data contracts and pipeline health; input and prediction distributions; delayed labels and slice-level performance; user or business impact.

Recalibrate policy: Adjust thresholds or calibration when prevalence or decision costs changed but labeled evidence shows the score ordering remains useful. Retrain a candidate: Use representative, quality-checked labels when the learned relationship changed.

variants.prompt: A feature distribution changes, but no outcomes have arrived yet. What can the team conclude?
